instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-28.10 Minimum wages (Virginia Minimum Wage Act)
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia, law.lis.virginia.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage greater of state rate or federal: 12.77 USD/h 2026-01-01 to 2027-01-01; 13.75 USD/h 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01; 15.00 USD/h 2028-01-01 to 2029-01-01; from 2029-01-01 adjusted annually by CPI-U (Commissioner sets by Oct 1, 2028 and annually; adjustment not below zero). Trainees in on-the-job programme up to 90 days: greater of federal minimum or 75% of state rate (12.77 x 0.75 = 9.5775 -> 9.58 USD/h 2026, derived; rounding not stated in statute). History: 2020 cc.1204,1242; 2026 cc.350,351.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-28.9 Definitions; tipped employee (three dated versions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum-wage 'employee' excludes (version until 2027-01-01): farm laborers; volunteers; golf caddies; commission outside salesmen, taxi drivers; under-18 employed by parent; inmates; summer-camp staff; under-16; students in bona fide educational programme; under-18 full-time students working <=20 h/week; full-time work-study students; babysitters <10 h/week; au pairs; H-2 temporary foreign workers (20 CFR 655); FLSA 213(a)(3) exempt. From 2027-01-01 (2026 cc.357,358) the farm-laborer exclusion is removed. Tipped employee = customarily receives > 30 USD/month in tips; tip credit = amount determined by employer (rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence); cannot classify as tipped where soliciting tips is prohibited. Wages include reasonable cost of customarily furnished meals and lodging.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-29 Time and medium of payment; withholding wages; written statement of earnings
figure_or_rule_carried: (B) regular pay periods: salaried at least monthly; hourly at least every two weeks or twice a month; monthly allowed for work-study students and, by agreement, employees whose weekly wages exceed 150% of the Commonwealth average weekly wage (65.2-500); on termination all wages paid on or before the next regular payday. (C) payment in cash, check, direct deposit to employee-designated account, or paycard with full fee disclosure and affirmative consent (paycard without consent only for hires after 2010-01-01 who do not designate an account, with one free withdrawal per pay period). (D) no deduction except taxes/law without written signed authorization; on each regular pay date a written statement by paystub or online accounting: employer name and address; hours worked (hourly, or salaried below the FLSA 13(a)(1) salary level); rate of pay; gross wages; amount and purpose of each deduction; sufficient to compute gross and net; keep 3 years from the work; agricultural employers only on request. (H) liquidated damages equal amount + 8% interest; (K) treble damages if knowing; (P, from 2026-07-01, 2026 c.1040) good-faith defense if cured within 14 days.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-29.2 Overtime: employer liability
figure_or_rule_carried: No separate state overtime standard: an employer violating FLSA overtime requirements is liable under 40.1-29(K); FLSA definitions, exemptions and overtime calculation methods apply; 3-year limitation. Result: overtime = FLSA 1.5x over 40 h/week, no daily overtime.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-33.3 Paid sick leave - definitions (home health workers)
figure_or_rule_carried: Paid sick leave article covers only 'home health workers' (consumer-directed personal care, respite or companion services under the state Medicaid plan) working on average >= 20 h/week or 90 h/month; paid at the normal hourly rate with same benefits, not below the 40.1-28.10 minimum wage without tip credit. Section history shows only 2021 Sp.Sess.I c.449 (no 2026 amendment).

instrument_name: Va. Code 63.2-1946 Employers to report new hires and new independent contractors
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); Virginia New Hire Reporting Center (DSS Division of Child Support Enforcement)
figure_or_rule_carried: Report each newly hired employee within 20 days of employment (as defined in 60.2-212) and each new independent contractor within 20 days of contract start; content = 42 USC 653a items only; by copy of W-4/W-9, electronic transmission in prescribed format or other means; electronic reporters: two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate employers may designate one state with notice to HHS and copy to the Center.

instrument_name: Va. Code 34-29 Maximum portion of disposable earnings subject to garnishment (two dated versions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary garnishment: lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or the excess over 40 x the greater of the federal or Virginia minimum hourly wage (2026: 40 x 12.77 = 510.80 USD/week protected, derived) - stricter than CCPA 30x. Support orders: 50% (supporting another spouse/child) / 60%, 55%/65% if arrears > 12 weeks. Limits do not apply to support orders, Chapter XIII bankruptcy, and (version until 2027-07-01) state or federal tax debts; version from 2027-07-01 (2026 c.396) lists only federal tax debts. No discharge for garnishment for any one indebtedness. Other pay periods: multiple set by Commissioner of Labor regulation.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); 510.80 derived arithmetically

instrument_name: Va. Code 59.1-443.2 Restricted use of social security numbers
figure_or_rule_carried: May not communicate an SSN to the general public, print it on an access card, require it alone for website access, or mail anything from which an SSN is visible outside or inside the envelope (relevant to mailed pay statements); embedding an SSN in a document is also barred; internal administrative use permitted. 40.1-29(D) does not list the SSN among pay-statement items; no Virginia truncation rule for pay statements located.

instrument_name: Va. Code 58.1-478 Employee wage statements; annual return; electronic filing
figure_or_rule_carried: Wage statement to each employee by January 31 (or on last payment if employment ends): employer name, employee name and SSN, total wages, total Virginia tax withheld. Annual return (VA-6) with copies of the statements due January 31, filed electronically in a format prescribed by the Tax Commissioner; waiver only for unreasonable burden, in writing.

instrument_name: Va. Code 20-79.3 Information required in income deduction order (child support)
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); DSS Division of Child Support Enforcement
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold the lesser of the ordered amount or the 34-29 maximum each regular pay period, starting with the next pay period after service; employer fee up to 5 USD per reply or remittance, withheld in addition to support; support orders have priority over other state-law liens; several support orders prorated on current amounts then arrears within 34-29 limits; remit on each pay date, or by EFT within 4 days of pay date, to DCSE; EFT mandatory for employers with 100+ employees and payroll processors with 50+ clients; notify DCSE promptly on termination with last address and new employer; combined single payment allowed; health coverage enrolment per order; 1,000 USD civil fine for discharge/discipline because of the order.

instrument_name: Va. Code 58.1-301 Conformity to Internal Revenue Code
figure_or_rule_carried: Fixed-date conformity: IRC as it existed on December 31, 2025 (2026 c.7; 2026 Sp.Sess.I c.1), plus later extensions of expiring provisions, except listed items (bonus depreciation, 5-year NOL carryback, AHYDO, 108(i), 68 itemized limitation pre-P.L.119-21, 10% medical floor, CARES 2303/2304/2306, CAA/ARPA loan-forgiveness items, P.L.119-21 70302 R&E and 70306 expensing, 280E for licensed cannabis from 2026). None of the exceptions concerns employee fringe-benefit exclusions (401(k), 125, HSA, 132 transit, 79 group-term life): Virginia follows the federal treatment for these.

instrument_name: Va. Code 60.2-213 Employment with hospital, higher education, state, subdivision, or religious/charitable organizations
figure_or_rule_carried: UI covers state and political-subdivision service and nonprofit (FUTA 3306(c)(8)) service where the organization had 4+ individuals in 20 weeks of the current or preceding year. Excluded: churches and church-controlled organizations; ordained/licensed ministers and members of religious orders in their ministry; sheltered rehabilitation work; work-relief programmes; inmates; elected officials, legislators, judiciary, National Guard, temporary emergency workers, major nontenured policymaking/advisory positions.

instrument_name: Virginia Income Tax Withholding Guide for Employers, 2614086 Rev. 10/26
article_or_section: pp.5 (standard deduction, due dates), 9-10 (forms), 11-13 (employees, reciprocity, nonresidents, VA-4), 14-16 (e-filing, penalties), 18-21 (records, tables, supplemental, formula)
figure_or_rule_carried: Re-read of the Rev. 10/26 guide already held under US-VA-P5-1-001 (same local file, not re-fetched). Additional rules carried: standard deduction 8,750/17,500 enacted 2025 is scheduled to sunset after Taxable Year 2026 and revert to 3,000/6,000; VA-4 mandatory, federal W-4 may not be substituted; no VA-4 -> withhold as zero exemptions; exemption claims renewed yearly; quarterly VA-5 due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31; monthly VA-5 by the 25th; VA-15 within 3 banking days of federal cutoff if accumulated > 500 USD; VA-16 quarterly reconciliation; VA-6 and W-2/1099 due Jan 31 (or within 30 days of last wages), W-2 via Web Upload in SSA EFW2 / IRS Pub 1220 format with state code 51, or eForms; all returns and payments electronic (waiver on request); late filing/payment penalty 6% per month, max 30%, min 10 USD; semi-weekly underpayment penalty 6%; records kept 3 years; tables rounded to nearest dollar, formula exact; supplemental paid with regular wages = aggregate; paid separately = aggregate method or flat 5.75% if tax withheld from regular wages; nonperiodic pension 4%; Virginia withholding applies where federal withholding applies (federal definition of wages); exempt: IRA/SEP, nonresident rail/motor/water carrier employees, merchant seamen, short-stay film crews; reciprocity KY and DC daily commuters; MD, PA, WV residents living in VA < 183 days with only wage income taxed by home state; residents of TN, NC and other states withheld; partially exempt employment half-time rule.
verification_method: inspected directly (PDF text extracted and read)

instrument_name: VEC FAQs - Employer UI tax (liability, rates, wage base, quarterly report, Web Upload, separation report)
article_or_section: Employer Profile; Tax rates; Filing; Web Upload Filing; Reimbursable vs Contributory
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: liable for FUTA, or quarterly payroll >= 1,500 USD, or an employee in 20 weeks in a calendar year; domestic employers when cash wages for domestic service >= 1,000 USD in a calendar quarter (annual filing option via ESS if quarterly payroll history < 5,000 USD, approval in advance); 501(c)(3) with < 4 employees in 20 weeks exempt. Localization: report where services are localized, else direction-and-control base. Base rates 0.1%-6.2%; new employer 2.5% plus add-ons; assigned 6.2% for no taxable payroll in 4 fiscal years, out-of-state construction contractors (3 years), delinquent employers; experience rate = benefit ratio over up to 4 fiscal years to June 30 applied to the Trust Fund balance factor; add-ons: pool cost charge (all employers, % not on page) and fund building charge 0.2% when trust fund balance <= 50%. Taxable wage base first 8,000 USD per employee per year (worked excess-wage example). UI gross wages = after section 125 deductions, before 401(k)/IRA-SEP/403(b) deductions; imputed group-term life over 50,000 USD differs from Medicare. Quarterly report due last day of the month after quarter end (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31), next business day if weekend/holiday, via ESS, eForm or Web Upload; late report penalty 100 USD per report (not for quarters with no wages); paper only with waiver. Web Upload file types: Excel, column-based MMREF/EFW2 and ICESA, delimited; amendments on paper FC-34 (or wagereconciliation@ for > 4 records). Separation: VEC sends Report of Separation and Wage Information to the last 30-day/240-hour employer via SIDES/ESS when a claim is filed. Page readable by curl 2026-11-02 (previously 403).

instrument_name: DOLI Payment of Wage - minimum wage FAQ
authority: Virginia Department of Labor and Industry (DOLI)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026-01-01 to 2027-01-01 minimum wage 12.77 USD/h; 13.75 USD/h from 2027-01-01; 15.00 USD/h from 2028-01-01 (second source for US-VAS5-001). Farm laborers covered from 2027-01-01. No sub-minimum wage certificates issued. Public-sector employees covered (not federal). Tipped employees: DOLI honours the FLSA tip credit, cash wage at least 2.13 USD/h, cash wage plus tips actually received must reach the Virginia minimum; tipped = > 30 USD/month in tips. No mandatory minimum-wage poster (optional notice).

instrument_name: Va. Code 60.2-806 Paid family and medical leave insurance program - Contributions
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); Virginia Employment Commission
figure_or_rule_carried: Contributions begin 2028-04-01; Commissioner fixes the rate by 2027-10-01 and annually (2028-2029 actuarial; from 2030 formula keeping fund >= 40% of expenditures). Employers of more than 10 employees deduct 50% (or a lesser agreed percentage) of the per-employee contribution from wages and remit the full contribution; employers of 10 or fewer deduct and remit only the 50% employee share. Deduction may not bring wages below minimum wage. Wage cap = Social Security contribution and benefit base (42 USC 430). Self-employed electing coverage pay the employer share. No contribution in 2026 or 2027.

instrument_name: VEC Virginia Paid Family & Medical Leave FAQ (April 22, 2026)
figure_or_rule_carried: Programme development 2026-2027; payroll contributions begin 2028-04-01; benefits available 2028-12-01; contribution split typically 50/50, employer may pay more; small businesses exempt from employer contribution; up to 12 weeks; benefit about 80% of weekly wage capped at 100% of statewide average weekly wage; private plan alternative with VEC approval. Retrieved via web.archive.org (VEC host returned F5 403 to curl 2026-11-02). Note: corrects the 'benefits begin 2028-04-01' wording in US-VA-P5-1-004 - benefits start 2028-12-01.

instrument_name: Va. Code 58.1-322.03 Virginia taxable income of residents - deductions (standard deduction, exemptions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Standard deduction (non-itemizers): TY2025-2026 8,750 single / 17,500 married; TY2027 9,200 / 18,400; TY2028-2029 9,300 / 18,600; TY2030 on 3,000 / 6,000 (MFS half). Personal exemption 930 each; additional 800 for each aged (65+) or blind taxpayer. History includes 2026 c.7 and 2026 Sp.Sess.I c.1. This SUPERSEDES the guide statement (Rev. 10/26, US-VAS5-013) that the 8,750/17,500 deduction sunsets after TY2026 and reverts to 3,000/6,000: the statute now carries 9,200 for 2027. Whether any revenue contingency attaches to items (vi)/(vii) in the enacting chapters was not read (open question).

instrument_name: Va. Code 2.2-4321.3 Prevailing wage rate; public works contracts
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); DOLI Commissioner
article_or_section: 2.2-4321.3 (definitions, C, F, H, J, L, N)
figure_or_rule_carried: Prevailing wage on public works of state agencies and covered institutions, and of localities that adopt an ordinance (C); rate set by Commissioner surveys every 3 years, never below Davis-Bacon; contracts of 250,000 USD or less excluded (N); contractor keeps wage/hour records and daily/weekly classification schedule 6 years, produce within 10 days and certify they reflect actual hours and pay (J); post rates on site and certify posting to Commissioner within 10 days (L); underpayment: wages + 8% interest and bid debarment (F). History adds 2026 cc.1014, 1040, 1060. Complements US-VA-P5-1-006.

instrument_name: Va. Code 60.2-212, 60.2-214, 60.2-219 UI employment, agricultural employment, exclusions
figure_or_rule_carried: Agricultural labor covered where employer paid >= 20,000 USD agricultural wages in a calendar quarter or employed 10+ agricultural workers in 20 weeks (current or preceding year); H-2A workers excluded but counted toward the threshold. Exclusions (60.2-219): federal employment; railroad; agricultural/domestic except as covered; employment by son/daughter/spouse and child under 21 employed by parent; 501(a) org with < 50 USD quarterly remuneration; students employed by their school; student nurses, interns; commission-only insurance agents, real estate salesmen, court reporters; direct sellers; taxi/executive sedan and courier drivers and barbers/cosmetologists excluded from FUTA; full-time students at organized camps; certain licensed therapists; inmates; non-business service under 50 USD per quarter.

instrument_name: Form VA-4 Employee's Virginia Income Tax Withholding Exemption Certificate, 2601064 Rev. 04/26
figure_or_rule_carried: Fields: SSN, name, address; 1(a) personal exemptions (self, spouse not claimed elsewhere, dependents), 1(b) age 65+/blindness exemptions, 1(c) total; 2 additional withholding; 3 exempt (instruction conditions); 4 exempt under SCRA/MSRRA (military spouse). File at hire; absent VA-4 -> withhold with no exemptions; employer may accept electronic VA-4 meeting 26 CFR 31.3402(f)(5)-1(c); employer reports suspected over-claims to Virginia Tax. Related forms VA-4B, VA-4P listed on the forms page.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-33.6:1 to 40.1-33.6:7 Paid Sick Leave (Article 2.1:1), effective July 1, 2027
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); DOLI Commissioner
figure_or_rule_carried: ENACTED, NOT YET IN FORCE (operating level: employer payroll/leave accrual). Covered employer phase-in: 50+ employees from 2027-07-01; 25+ from 2028-01-01; 1+ from 2029-01-01; includes the Commonwealth and political subdivisions; home health workers stay under 40.1-33.3. Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked from start of employment; carry-over; accrual and use capped at 40 hours per year (employer-defined 12-month year) unless employer sets higher; FLSA 13(a)(1)-exempt employees deemed 40 h/week (or normal shorter week); front-load of 40 hours satisfies accrual; PTO policy or CBA meeting the standard suffices; no payout on separation; reinstatement if rehired within 12 months unless paid out; successor employer carries balances; employer may advance leave. Paid at the regular rate as defined in 40.1-29.3(B), not below the 40.1-28.10 minimum without tip credit. Use: increments no greater than 4 hours; documentation only for 3+ consecutive work days. Commissioner regulations: written notice and posting, 3-year records of accrual and use, confidentiality. Longshore CBA exemption until CBA expiry or 2030-12-31.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-29.3 Overtime for certain employees (derivative air carriers; home care direct support)
figure_or_rule_carried: State overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/week for employees of derivative air carriers (Railway Labor Act) and home-care agency/third-party direct support service workers. Regular rate = hourly rate plus other non-overtime wages paid or allocated for the workweek, excluding FLSA regular-rate exclusions, divided by total hours worked. This regular-rate definition is also the pay basis for paid sick leave from 2027-07-01 (40.1-33.6:1). History 2022 cc.461,462; 2026 c.1040.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-28.7:12 Wage or salary history ban; pay range transparency (2026 cc.996, 1063)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer may not seek or rely on salary history; must disclose the wage/salary or good-faith range in each public and internal posting (hiring, promotion, transfer); civil penalty up to 1,000 USD first and 5,000 USD subsequent; private action within 1 year; 15-business-day cure for posting defects. Not a payroll-calculation item (HR/recruiting); recorded for completeness. Effective date taken as the default 2026-07-01 for 2026 Acts (enacting-clause dates not read).
